// @leetvim id=284 slug=peeking-iterator lang=cpp
// 284. Peeking Iterator (Medium)
// https://leetcode.com/problems/peeking-iterator/

// Below is the interface for Iterator, which is already defined for you.
class Iterator {
		struct Data;
		Data* data;
public:
		Iterator(const vector<int>& nums);
		Iterator(const Iterator& iter);

		// Returns the next element in the iteration.
		int next();

		// Returns true if the iteration has more elements.
		bool hasNext() const;
	};

# @leetvim id=284 slug=peeking-iterator lang=python3
# 284. Peeking Iterator (Medium)
# https://leetcode.com/problems/peeking-iterator/

# Below is the interface for Iterator, which is already defined for you.
class Iterator:
    def __init__(self, nums):
        """
        Initializes an iterator object to the beginning of a list.
        :type nums: List[int]
        """
        raise NotImplementedError

    def hasNext(self) -> Any:
        """
        Returns true if the iteration has more elements.
        :rtype: bool
        """
        raise NotImplementedError

    def next(self) -> Any:
        """
        Returns the next element in the iteration.
        :rtype: int
        """
        raise NotImplementedError

=== python
# @leetvim id=284 slug=peeking-iterator lang=python
# 284. Peeking Iterator (Medium)
# https://leetcode.com/problems/peeking-iterator/

# Below is the interface for Iterator, which is already defined for you.
class Iterator(object):
    def __init__(self, nums):
        """
        Initializes an iterator object to the beginning of a list.
        :type nums: List[int]
        """
        raise NotImplementedError

    def hasNext(self) -> Any:
        """
        Returns true if the iteration has more elements.
        :rtype: bool
        """
        raise NotImplementedError

    def next(self) -> Any:
        """
        Returns the next element in the iteration.
        :rtype: int
        """
        raise NotImplementedError

// This is the Iterator's API interface.
// You should not implement it, or speculate about its implementation
declare class Iterator {
     hasNext(): boolean;

     next(): number;
}
export {}; // a module, so these names are its own

package main

// Below is the interface for Iterator, which is already defined for you.
type Iterator struct {}

// Returns true if the iteration has more elements.
func (this *Iterator) hasNext() bool { panic("") }

// Returns the next element in the iteration.
func (this *Iterator) next() int { panic("") }
